questions.prompt: Order the main steps of a cold HTTPS page load, from URL to content.

items.text: Routing decision + ARP for the gateway

questions.explanation: Resolve the name, decide the next hop (and ARP for it), establish TCP, secure it with TLS, then exchange HTTP.

questions.prompt: When your laptop sends a request to a remote server, whose MAC address is the destination in the first frame?

options.text: The default gateway's MAC (the next hop)

questions.explanation: The server is remote, so the frame goes to the default gateway first; its MAC (found via ARP) is the destination, while the destination IP is the server's.

questions.prompt: What does NAT do to the reply packets coming back to your laptop?

options.text: Translates the public destination back to your private address using its mapping
Drops them because they are inbound

questions.explanation: NAT recorded the outbound mapping, so it reverses it on replies — translating the public destination back to your private IP/port so the reply reaches your laptop.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the end-to-end flow are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: DNS resolution happens before any TCP connection is made
The destination IP stays the same end-to-end while the MAC changes each hop
A cold load takes several round trips before content arrives
The TLS handshake happens before the TCP handshake

questions.explanation: DNS comes first, the IP is stable while MAC changes per hop, and a cold load is multi-RTT. TLS runs after TCP is established, not before.

questions.prompt: Match each step of the flow to the tool that inspects it.
questions.explanation: dig checks DNS, traceroute maps the path, curl -v shows the handshakes and HTTP, and tcpdump reveals the actual packets.

questions.prompt: Because a cold load needs multiple sequential round trips, its startup time is dominated by ____, not bandwidth.
questions.explanation: DNS, TCP, TLS, and HTTP each cost round trips, so latency (RTT) dominates a cold load — more bandwidth won't shorten those trips.
